hero.subtitle: A car crash on SR-91, Ball Road or Lincoln Avenue can upend an ordinary week in Anaheim. We handle Orange County car accident claims at no cost unless you recover.

about.title: Anaheim Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Anaheim moves a lot of people every day. Between the resort area and the daily flow along SR-91 in both directions, the city recorded 2,161 injury collisions in 2025. Those crashes left 3,162 people injured and took 34 lives. Ball Road and Lincoln Avenue also appear again and again in the public collision records, and the numbers tend to climb on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the week's commute meets weekend traffic. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered. Medical visits, a car that won't run, calls from an adjuster you didn't ask to hear from. We're here to help you through it. Our team handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we'll review your case and advise you on your options. The choice of whether to move forward stays with you.

items.title: The two-year clock is shorter than it sounds
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim involving a city vehicle or a state-maintained road like SR-91 may require a government claim within six months. We can sort out which deadline applies to you before it becomes a problem.

items.title: Being partly at fault doesn't end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some of the blame; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. That matters in the kind of multi-car freeway situations Anaheim sees regularly.

items.title: Evidence and recorded statements
items.desc: Photos, dash-cam footage, witness names and repair estimates fade or disappear quickly. We typically advise against giving the other driver's insurer a recorded statement until you've had a chance to talk with us, and we work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the 91 near the Orange County line. Does it matter which agency handled the report?
items.answer: It can. Freeway collisions in Anaheim are often handled by the CHP rather than Anaheim PD, and the report is requested through a different office. We can track down the correct report and, if a public agency's road condition or vehicle played a role, flag the shorter six-month government claim deadline early.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called me. What should I say?
items.answer: You are not required to give them a recorded statement, and we suggest you don't until you've spoken with us. Be polite, take down the adjuster's name and claim number, and say you'll be in touch. Keep your own notes, photos and medical paperwork together in the meantime.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For an ordinary car accident claim, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering or loss of enjoyment of life. What you may recover depends on the facts of your case, your injuries and the available insurance coverage. No one can promise a particular result; we simply evaluate your situation and advise you on your options.
